Unified product design direction

Make every tap understandable.

A clearer path from permission to preview to action, while keeping TapThatX recognizably native.

Compare the designs
Preserve the interaction. Improve the explanation.

The glass ring, coordinated mint palette, system typography, five settings sections, seven command positions and deliberate tap timing remain the foundation.

One direction, reconciled from both reviews.

This document merges the independent review with the earlier design document, using the accepted decisions from their comparison. Both originals remain intact.

A capable utility with competing signals.

The main design debt is understanding readiness, not inventing a new visual identity.

“Is it listening, did it recognize my tap, and will it run an action?”

These are separate questions. Give each a stable place and a plain answer.

Major

Readiness is distributed across the window.

Pause, Enable system actions, the graph’s live status and the footer describe different layers of state. A prominent preview banner and a consequence-aware footer make the relationship explicit. This is a comprehension finding, not proof of accidental execution.

Major

The visual emphasis favors signal over outcome.

Tuning makes the graph the largest element. Retain it for diagnosis, but promote waiting, recognized, settling and disconnected states into readable text outside the plot.

Major

The ring is recognizable but text is small.

At its defined size, 10 pt labels and translucent material are a legibility risk. Increase type and compare a stable backing against varied desktops before retaining blur.

Polish

Precision and save consequences need consistency.

Use 0.0175 g everywhere for the same threshold. Bring dataset replacement wording next to Save dataset, where the user makes the decision.

Put recognition ahead of the waveform.

Tuning / native render comparison

Implementation boundary

Preserve the 800 Hz baseline and all rate options. Add a plain graph legend and visible drag/arrow-key guidance. Use matching precision for the same threshold; axis ticks may use fewer decimals. Keep unvalidated presets out of the default controls.

Evidence: SetupView.swift:64, MotionGraphView.swift:99

Make the next required action unmistakable.

Permissions / native render comparison

Implementation boundary

Both examples show Accessibility missing and Input Monitoring allowed. Permission gating is a proposed behavior change: distinguish system-action requirements from typing suppression, and keep safe preview available.

Evidence: PermissionSetupView.swift:9, SetupView.swift:43

Teach the ring at the point of choice.

Actions / native render comparison

Implementation boundary

The native example shows Ring selected. Direct actions need their own consequence text. ChatGPT choices must retain their Experimental label and Check controls action. Do not invent app compatibility.

Evidence: SetupView.swift:101, TapThatXApp.swift:73

Keep the signature. Clarify the state.

Command ring / native render comparison

Implementation boundary

Keep all seven positions, clockwise order, keyboard navigation and Escape cancellation. Short labels are presentation-only: stored raw values and full accessibility names stay unchanged. Keep hints available; do not fade them based on elapsed usage.

Evidence: RadialPanelController.swift:146, Models.swift:23

Explain the recording and the save consequence.

Recordings / native render comparison

Implementation boundary

Keep the 15-second duration, activity choices, intended-pair count and dataset selection. The preview uses static field values. Before replacing an existing saved dataset, show a confirmation with Cancel and Replace dataset.

Evidence: SetupView.swift:130, DiagnosticsStore.swift

Make troubleshooting a short path.

Advanced / native render comparison

Implementation boundary

Retain Direct sensor, Sensor helper and Simulated input, all helper controls and raw event details. Help disclosures must not conceal an active connection failure. Saving stays local.

Evidence: SetupView.swift:182, TapThatXApp.swift:77

Design the states, not just the happy path.

These working examples show proposed presentation logic. They never connect to the app, sensor, permissions or system actions.

Readiness language

Keep recognition status distinct from action availability. A disabled action should explain the next step.

Preview mode

You can test taps here. System actions are paused while settings are open.

Recognition
Listening
System actions
Paused for settings

Next step: Enable & close when you finish testing.

Recognition feedback

Show the outcome without asking people to interpret a waveform. Each button displays a controlled example.

Waiting for a double-tap

Keep still briefly, then tap twice. Preview mode will not run an action.

“Ignored near typing” requires a confirmed suppression event. Never infer rejection reasons from graph peaks. Keep the last confirmed result visible until a new result or reset, with an event timestamp.

State precedence proposal: show all active blockers in details; choose the actionable headline from recording, user pause, connection/access problems, simulation or low rate, then settings preview. Preserve the existing action guards. Inactive-session, calibration and starting states are included in the examples; test combined blockers against the actual lifecycle before implementation.

Make the outcome visible.

The earlier review’s strongest addition: readable acknowledgments, compact ring labels, and feedback close to the action.

Keep recovery retrievable

A longer timeout alone is insufficient. Retain the error and recovery instruction in the relevant settings area or recent activity until superseded or dismissed. Do not turn the existing noninteractive toast into an unlabeled clickable surface.

Feedback marker example

Inside Advanced, prefer this confirmation inline beside Missed tap and False trigger. An optional toast must not become the only confirmation.

Short labels, explicit scope

The center names ChatGPT and its experimental status when an assistant action is selected. Keep “Approve once,” full accessible labels, and all persisted command values. A sparkle alone does not communicate experimental status.

One source of current status

Keep the native menu. Present recognition and action availability separately from commands, and prefix historical feedback with “Recent” plus its timestamp. Hide the footer’s secondary sentence when it duplicates the main status. A diagnostic marker acknowledgment means it was added to the session log, not that a dataset was exported to disk.

One native visual system.

Mint carries identity. Typography, grouping and state labels carry meaning.

Color and materials

The current ring defines mint as RGB 0.38 / 0.83 / 0.72. Keep that identity on dark surfaces; use a deeper related green for readable controls on light surfaces. Status must also have text or an icon.

Existing ring mint#61D4B8, rounded from source
Proposed light accent#1F7561, control emphasis
Document light surface#F6F8F7
Document dark surface#131C18

App surfaces use semantic macOS colors. Graph amber remains a functional threshold color. Glass remains the default ring material, with a restrained dark backing and an opaque Reduce Transparency fallback. Contrast must be checked over bright, dark and busy desktops; no wallpaper-independent guarantee is made.

Type, spacing and interaction

  • Type: system font; 24 pt page titles, 13 pt body, 12 pt helper copy. Ring: 12 pt sector labels and 17 pt selected title.
  • Spacing: 20–24 pt page insets; 12–16 pt between related controls; larger separation between tasks. Preserve scroll access at the 720 × 640 minimum.
  • Shape: 10 pt grouped regions in the app; native button shapes. The ring is the only circular command surface.
  • Motion: retain the 450 ms single-tap window, 220 ms ring commit and approximately 620 ms direct-action sequence. Do not tune detection timing as a styling change.
  • Accessibility: preserve keyboard cycling, selected traits, graph adjustment, Reduce Motion and Reduce Transparency. Verify VoiceOver announcements and focus return.

Dark appearance comparison

Fresh native renders check hierarchy in dark appearance. Screenshot colors are fixed evidence; the document’s Appearance button changes the surrounding document.

Turn the direction into small, testable changes.

These are proposed app changes. This delivery changes documentation and review artifacts only.

Work itemChange and locationAcceptance criterion
Readiness and permissions

Highest priority

Coordinate SetupView, PermissionSetupView and AppModel. Present recognition and action state separately; derive the footer from the actual next action.Every disabled state has a reason and recovery. No Ready claim when the sensor is disconnected. Preview remains safe. Recheck permissions on return without duplicate prompts.
Tuning feedback

Highest priority

Promote confirmed recognition state above MotionGraphView. Bind graph drag, keyboard input and proposed slider to the same threshold; retain clamping and experimental options.All controls show four-decimal g values and stay in sync. Settling, empty trace, pause and sensor failure are distinguishable. New feedback cannot claim an unobserved rejection reason.
Ring legibility

Next

Adjust RingView type, glass backing and selection emphasis. Add presentation-only short labels and explicit preview/assistant context. Keep command identifiers and geometry.Seven labels fit at 460 pt without overlap. Test bright, dark and busy desktops, reduced transparency and reduced motion. Preview cannot execute; Escape and focus loss cancel pending actions.
Actions and recordings

Next

Group gesture guidance around Preview ring. Move save consequence next to Save dataset; confirm replacement when a dataset exists.Every action choice has accurate instructions. Recording, early stop, empty, saved and failed-save states are visible. Canceling replacement leaves the existing file untouched.
Acknowledgments

Next

Separate kind, message, optional filename and recovery text in AcknowledgmentController. Keep save/error details in persistent context; confirm markers inline.Success, error and informational messages have text and distinct symbols. Long paths wrap or shorten without hiding access to the full value. Repeated messages replace cleanly; stale timers cannot dismiss a newer message. Verify VoiceOver announcement without stealing focus.
Diagnostics and menu

Follow-through

Reuse the existing recent-activity export on Advanced. Retain the native menu and its labels; align its status wording with settings.Missed tap → Save last 15 seconds is discoverable. Empty events and export failures have explicit text. File saving remains local and no new telemetry is introduced.

Behavior to preserve

  • Actions pause in settings and recordings; simulation uses dry runs.
  • All existing action choices and experimental caveats remain available.
  • Single tap moves after the double-tap window; double-tap selects without advancing first.
  • Arrow navigation wraps; Return chooses; Escape and focus loss cancel.
  • Recordings do not automatically train the detector. Sensor compatibility and lower-rate reliability remain unproven beyond existing evidence.

Validation before app implementation ships

  • Tests for footer/readiness derivation, simultaneous blockers, permission return and disconnected sensor.
  • Regression checks for tap timing, preview safety and cancellation during commit.
  • Threshold synchronization and clamp boundaries; replacement-cancel and failed-save paths.
  • Visual review at 720 × 640 and 760 × 800, in both appearances, with long status text.
  • VoiceOver, keyboard-only operation, increased contrast, reduced motion and transparency on the real app.

Decisions that resolve the two reviews.

This is one implementation direction. Experiments are separated from changes ready to specify.

TopicUnified decisionReason
Ring material and labelsGlass by default; opaque accessibility fallback. Short sector labels, stronger selection, full context in the hub.Preserves character while improving reading and command scope. Evaluate the backing on real desktops before finalizing opacity.
Settings navigationKeep the five existing sections and segmented navigation in the implementation baseline. Prototype a sidebar separately at 720 × 640.A sidebar may help scanning, but its width cost must be tested. Five segments alone do not prove failure.
Threshold controlsAdd the legend and visible adjustment guidance. Use four decimals for every display of the threshold, while keeping readable axis ticks.Fixes discoverability and inconsistent values. “Light / Balanced / Firm” needs tested behavior before being offered as presets.
Readiness and footerExplicit preview state, independent recognition/action status, inline blocker recovery, and “Pause recognition” everywhere. Keep “Enable & close.”The existing label names both effects more clearly than “Finish & enable.” Changing the words alone does not resolve blocked states.
Token consistencyUse semantic roles within one mint family, retaining distinct waveform, selection, and light-surface emphasis colors.Consistency means an intentional mapping, not one hex value regardless of background and purpose.
Recordings and feedbackExplain replacement next to Save dataset. Make activity-driven count changes explicit. Confirm markers inline; keep errors retrievable.A changed activity can justify a new expected count. Silently resetting or blindly preserving a stale count can both mislead.

Prototype before adopting

  • Sidebar navigation at minimum and normal window sizes.
  • Threshold presets validated against labeled recordings.
  • Optional grouping of assistant actions without moving established command positions.
  • A guided first-use sequence that retains direct access to settings.

Do not carry forward

  • Automatic hint removal after a week or a fixed number of opens.
  • Sparkle-only experimental labels or “Approve” without “once.”
  • Untested per-command haptic intensity, arbitrary toast-duration formulas, or claims of guaranteed contrast over every wallpaper.
  • “No layout risk” claims and fixed half-day estimates for behavior changes.

Build in dependency order

State and copy

Establish accurate status first.

Define recognition and action presentation states; deduplicate footer text; align pause wording. Add tests for simultaneous blockers, permission return and sensor loss.

Visual components

Apply the unified ring and feedback treatment.

Introduce presentation-only command labels, state-aware hub copy, semantic color roles, structured acknowledgments and visible threshold guidance. Preserve gesture timing and cancellation guards.

Flow refinement

Make recording and diagnosis understandable.

Implement replacement confirmation, explicit expected-count resets, marker feedback and timestamped recent acknowledgments. Test failure and cancellation paths.

Evaluate alternatives

Use evidence to decide the structural changes.

Test sidebar space, readability over varied desktops, long messages and keyboard use. Only adopt presets or layout changes when they improve real tasks.

Skills and iteration

Design Taste Frontend guides the document: preserved identity, one coordinated palette, measured spacing, native image evidence and repeated visual review. Its landing-page conventions do not dictate macOS settings. UX Peak supplies the problem → consequence → fix method. UI UX Pro Max’s useful feedback and accessibility findings are retained; its generic neumorphism and blue/orange recommendation remains rejected.

Document dials: variance 5 / motion 2 / density 5. The synthesis updates the native ring, adds acknowledgment examples, and revises Tuning guidance. Current/proposed figures use controlled native rendering, rather than mixing screenshot sizes or obscuring settings with an open ring. Browser verification covers navigation, image enlargement, state examples and narrow layouts.

Native fixture changes were limited to selecting the settings page, supplying an inert model and rendering it. No sensor samples were fabricated. The source views’ system material and control styling can differ from a frontmost installed app. Proposed recordings and diagnostics fields are visual examples, not full working app screens. The toast fixture uses the source’s Text/material presentation and an example filename; the new toast layouts are separate prototypes.

General platform reference: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Settings. Its guidance on app-specific settings informed retaining a focused native settings area. The unified decisions above synthesize the source audit, both documents and the accepted reconciliation.
